title: Boundary-unit factorization in a regular local ring
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], hence Noetherian, and let $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ be members at distinct positions of a regular system of parameters of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], with $r\ge0$. Then $A$ is an integral domain with unique factorization: every nonzero element is a unit times a finite product of prime elements, uniquely up to order and association. Each $t_i$ is prime. Put $T=t_1\cdots t_r$, with empty product $1$, and write $A[1/T]$ for localization at the powers of $T$. An element $f\in A$ becomes a unit in $A[1/T]$ if and only if $f=u\prod_{i=1}^r t_i^{a_i}$ for a unit $u\in A^\times$ and integers $a_i\ge0$.

source.place: Tag 0AG0, lemma-regular-local-UFD (lines 36800–36858): a regular local ring is a UFD; its proof first explains that a member of a regular parameter system is prime. The localization-unit clause is the elementary consequence of unique factorization detailed in report.md, rather than an assertion of the normal-crossings equivalence lemma.

proof.text: The regular-local and parameter-list hypotheses are exactly [def-weil-regular-scheme] and [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Applying [lem-sc-regular-local-domain] to A gives that A is a nonzero integral domain. Each t_i lies in the maximal ideal because the list generates it.

source.place: Tag 0AG0, proof opening: a regular local ring is a domain

proof.text: Write d=dim A. The parameter list has length d and generates m. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], the cotangent space m/m^2 has dimension d. The images of the d parameters span that d-dimensional space; [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] identifies generation modulo m with generation of m, so these images form a basis. In particular each t_i is outside m^2.

proof.text: For every $i$, Step 2 gives $t_i\in\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak m^2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-hypersurface-criterion] the quotient $A/(t_i)$ is a regular local ring, hence an integral domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. Also $t_i\ne0$, since $0\in\mathfrak m^2$. Hence $(t_i)$ is a proper nonzero prime ideal, i.e. $t_i$ is a prime element.

proof.text:
Induction claim: for every $d\ge0$, every regular local ring of dimension $d$ is a unique factorization domain in the sense of [lem-trf-ufd-height-one](i). Base $d=0$: the maximal ideal is generated by the empty list, so $A$ is a field and every nonzero element is a unit (empty product). Inductive step, $d>0$: by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] $\dim\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2=d>0$, so there is $x\in\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak m^2$; exactly as in Step 3, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-hypersurface-criterion] and [lem-sc-regular-local-domain] make $x$ a prime element. Let $\mathfrak p$ be a height-one prime of $A$. If $x\in\mathfrak p$, then $0\subsetneq(x)\subseteq\mathfrak p$ with $(x)$ prime, so height one forces $\mathfrak p=(x)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] $A_{\mathfrak q'}$ is regular local, so by the induction hypothesis it is a unique factorization domain, and it is a Noetherian domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. If $\mathfrak p

In both cases $(\mathfrak p_x)_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak q'}$ is a nonzero principal ideal of a domain, i.e. free of rank one. Since $A_x$ is Noetherian, the ideal $\mathfrak p_x$ is finitely generated, hence finitely presented.

proof.text: By Step 4 and [lem-trf-finite-projective-local-free], $\mathfrak p_x$ is a finitely generated projective $A_x$-module whose localization at every prime of $A_x$ is free of rank one. By [lem-trf-regular-local-pic-zero] applied to $A$ and $x$, $\mathfrak p_x\cong A_x$; the image $y$ of $1$ generates, so $\mathfrak p_x=(y)$ with $y\in A_x$.

Since $\mathfrak p$ is prime, some $a_i\in\mathfrak p$, so $a_i\in\mathfrak p_x=(y)$ and $y\mid a_i$ in $A_x$; also $a_i\mid f$, and $x$ is a unit of $A_x$, so $a_i\mid y$ in $A_x$. Then $0\subsetneq(a_i)\subseteq\mathfrak p$ with $(a_i)$ prime and $\mathfrak p$ of height one, hence $(a_i)=\mathfrak p$. This completes the inductive step: every height-one prime of $A$ is principal, and [lem-trf-ufd-height-one] makes $A$ a unique factorization domain.

proof.text: By the induction of Steps 4–6, applied to $A$ of dimension $d$, and since $A$ is a Noetherian domain by Step 1, [lem-trf-ufd-height-one] shows that $A$ is a unique factorization domain: every nonzero element is a unit times a finite product of prime elements, uniquely up to order and association.

Suppose $f$ is a unit in $A[1/T]$. By the definition of localization, $fg=T^n$ for some $g\in A$ and $n\ge0$ (an equality in $A$ because $A$ is a domain and $T\ne0$ by Steps 1 and 3). Hence $f\ne0$; factor $f$ in the UFD of Step 7. Every prime factor $p$ of $f$ divides $T^n=t_1^n\cdots t_r^n$, hence divides some $t_i$; as $t_i$ is prime, hence irreducible, and $p$ is a nonunit, $p$ is associated to $t_i$. Grouping associates yields $f=u\prod_it_i^{a_i}$ with $u\in A^\times$ and $a_i\ge0$; for $r=0$ there is no prime factor and $f=u$.

source.place: Tag 0AG0, followed by the elementary localization calculation

proof.text: Conversely, if f=u prod_i t_i^{a_i}, choose n>=max_i a_i (n=0 when r=0). Then T^n/f=u^{-1} prod_i t_i^{n-a_i} lies in A, so f has inverse g/T^n in A[1/T]. For r=0, T=1 and the criterion says exactly that f is a unit of A.

lean.statement: theorem regularLocalUFDBoundaryFactorization (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsRegularLocalRing A] (t : List A) (ht : IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters t) (r : ℕ) (ι : Fin r → Fin t.length) (hι : Function.Injective ι) : IsDomain A ∧ UniqueFactorizationMonoid A ∧ (∀ i : Fin r, Prime (t.get (ι i))) ∧ (∀ f : A, IsUnit (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (∏ i : Fin r, t.get (ι i))) f) ↔ ∃ u : A, IsUnit u ∧ ∃ a : Fin r → ℕ, f = u * ∏ i : Fin r, (t.get (ι i)) ^ (a i))
